guides.title: Flood
guides.summary: Before, during and after a flood
steps: Move important documents, medicines and phone chargers to a waterproof bag now, before water rises.
Know your building's highest safe floor and the fastest route to it.
If water is rising, move to higher ground immediately — do not wait for it to enter your home.
Never walk or drive through moving flood water. 15cm of fast water can knock an adult down.
Avoid contact with flood water where possible — it can be contaminated.
After the flood, do not return home until authorities say it is safe. Check for structural damage before entering.
Boil or treat drinking water until you know the local supply is safe again.

guides.title: Fire
guides.summary: Before, during and after a fire emergency
steps: Know two exit routes from your home or building, not just one.
Keep a fire extinguisher and a torch somewhere you can reach in the dark.
If you smell smoke, stay low — cleaner air is near the floor.
Check doors for heat before opening them. If a door is hot, use your second exit.
Never use a lift during a fire — always take the stairs.
Once outside, stay outside. Do not go back in for belongings.
Call emergency services as soon as you are safe, and use SETU's SOS if the network is down.

guides.title: Earthquake
guides.summary: Before, during and after an earthquake
steps: Identify solid furniture near you (a sturdy table, an interior wall corner) you could shelter under or against.
Secure heavy furniture and shelves that could fall.
When shaking starts: Drop, Cover, Hold On. Get under sturdy furniture and hold on until shaking stops.
Stay away from windows, mirrors and anything that could shatter.
If outdoors, move to an open area away from buildings, trees and power lines.
After shaking stops, expect aftershocks. Check yourself and others for injuries before moving around.
Exit the building calmly if it is damaged — do not use lifts.

guides.title: Accident / General Emergency
guides.summary: What to do at the scene of an accident
steps: Check for danger to yourself before approaching — oncoming traffic, fire, unstable structures.
Call for help immediately. Use SETU's SOS if you have no signal.
Do not move an injured person unless they are in immediate danger (fire, traffic, flood).
If someone is bleeding heavily, apply firm, steady pressure with a clean cloth.
Keep the person calm and still until help arrives.
Note the location clearly — a nearby landmark helps responders find you faster.

guides.title: Women's Safety
guides.summary: Staying safe and reaching help quickly
steps: Share your live location with a trusted contact when travelling alone, especially at night.
Keep SETU's SOS quick-access enabled — a hold or volume-button trigger can call for help silently.
Trust your instincts. If a situation feels wrong, move to a public, well-lit place.
Memorise or save at least two emergency contacts who can act quickly.
If you are being followed, head toward the nearest open shop, guard post or crowd, not home.

guides.title: Child Safety
guides.summary: Preparing children and reporting a missing child
steps: Teach children their full name, a parent's phone number, and how to find a trusted adult (police, guard, shopkeeper) if lost.
Add your child's profile in SETU's Child Safety section so it's ready if needed.
Agree on a family meeting point in case you get separated during an emergency.
If a child goes missing, report it immediately — do not wait. Use SETU's lost child broadcast to alert nearby devices.
Give a clear, recent description: height, clothing, and where they were last seen.

guides.title: Senior Citizen Emergency
steps: Keep a list of current medications, dosages and doctor contact details somewhere accessible.
Save emergency contacts in SETU with clear labels (e.g. "Son — Ravi").
If a senior lives alone, agree on a daily check-in method with family.
Know the route to the nearest hospital and keep it saved offline.
During a disaster, mobility may be limited — plan an evacuation route that does not rely on stairs where possible.
